questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Fleming single-handedly turned penicillin into a mass-produced drug
The discovery and development of penicillin, from early clues to mass production
The rise of antibiotic resistance after penicillin entered widespread use
How botanists classified Penicillium moulds throughout the 20th century
questions.explain: It traces penicillin from early mould observations through Fleming, the Oxford team and wartime production.

questions.q: Which bacterium was NOT killed by Fleming's mould?
options: Staphylococcus
Streptococcus
Diphtheria bacillus
Typhoid bacterium
questions.explain: Typhoid bacterium and H. influenzae were unaffected.

options: Ernst Chain
Dorothy Hodgkin
Mary Ethel Florey
Norman Heatley
questions.explain: Dorothy Hodgkin determined its structure, earning the 1964 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

questions.q: Where did consensus say the contaminating mould spores came from?
options: The open window facing Praed Street
Fleming's own vacation home
A research student's culture
La Touche's laboratory a floor below
questions.explain: A consensus developed that the mould came from La Touche's laboratory, a floor below Fleming's.

questions.q: What does the passage imply about Fleming's discovery?
options: It depended partly on fortunate laboratory temperatures
It was immediately recognized and hailed by the scientific community
It was the first ever observation of a mould killing bacteria
It required deliberately seeding the plate with a Penicillium mould
questions.explain: It notes fortuitously cool then warmer August temperatures favoured first the mould and then the bacteria.
